newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end up on textiles, seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end up on textiles, seen mixed.

text.p: Pakistani stocks closed up on Tuesday amid speculative buying mainly in textile in anticipation of a relief package the caretaker government is likely to announce for the textile industry, dealers said.
But they said the market might open mixed on Wednesday as the rise could attract profit-taking, mainly by foreign funds.
The government is likely to revise import duties on cotton and synthetic fibres not produced in Pakistan to help the textile industry cope with a domestic cotton crop shortfall.
The Karachi Stock Exchange 100-share index rose 8.63 points, or 0.58 percent, to end at 1,490. Gainers led losers 242 to 95.
Turnover fell to 43.57 million shares from Monday's 48.97 million.
Saif Textile rose 1.0 to 15, Ellcot Spinning 1.0 to 6.75, Gadoon Textile 2.75 to 38.50, Pakistan State Oil 3.0 to 393 and Fauji Fertilizer 0.50 to 77.50. Hub Power fell 0.30 to 35.50.
